name: Waterloo International
features: 400 m train shed that curves and tapers with the tracks, on asymmetric three-pin bowstring arches.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1994

photos.file: File:The Eurostar terminus at Waterloo - geograph.org.uk - 2017939.jpg
File:Looking up at the former Waterloo International station from Leake Street - geograph.org.uk - 6270938.jpg

note: Now platforms 20-24 of Waterloo station. Fourth photo is a close-up of the glazing and blue trusses.

name: Netherlands Embassy, Berlin
features: A continuous route, the 'trajectory', winds up through the cube from entrance to roof terrace.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2005

photos.file: File:Embassy of the Netherlands in Berlin November 2013.jpg
File:Berlin - Botschaft des Königreichs der Niederlande.jpg

note: Also Category:Dutch Embassy, Berlin.

name: MUSAC, Museum of Contemporary Art of Castilla y León
features: Plan of repeated square and rhomboid cells; coloured glass facade drawn from León Cathedral's stained glass.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2007
note: Exterior photos are in Category:Exterior of the MUSAC.

name: DeFlat Kleiburg
features: A 1970s Bijlmermeer slab of 500 flats saved from demolition; residents buy bare shells and fit them out.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2017
note: 2015 photos may show the slab mid-renovation; the 2021 one is after.

name: Banco Borges & Irmão
features: Small white bank on a corner, its curved wall turning the street; the first Mies van der Rohe Award.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1988

photos.file: File:Banco Borges e Irmão Vila do Conde 2011.jpg
File:Vila do Conde Bank by Álvaro Siza photo by Christian Gänshirt.jpg

note: No Commons category; both files found by search. Second photo is a close side view with the entrance stair.

name: Palau Municipal d'Esports de Badalona
features: Oval arena built for basketball at the 1992 Olympics, one roof spanning the whole seating bowl.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1992
note: Weak set: the only exterior photos are one distant view from a hill (and its crop, 1423x1174). Other files are interiors.

name: Study Pavilion, TU Braunschweig
features: A light steel frame of open, fully glazed study floors with outside stairs, built to be taken apart.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2024

photos.file: File:Studierendenhaus der Technischen Universität Braunschweig MH-GD 1287.jpeg

note: German name: Studierendenhaus der TU Braunschweig. Both seen photos are dusk/night views.

name: Palais des Expositions (Grand Palais), Charleroi
by: AgwA, architecten jan de vylder inge vinck
features: 1950s exhibition halls kept and opened up: facades taken off so the central hall becomes a covered public foyer.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2026
note: Completion year not confirmed by a source (CC0 photos from 2024 show it finished); check before publishing. Original 1954 building by Joseph Tirou and Octave Pinkers. Many more CC0 2023-24 photos in the category.

name: Stadthaus Scharnhauser Park
features: Town hall whose upper floors overhang the square as a deep canopy, with a field of light rods in front.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003, Emerging Architect special mention
note: Only two files, no category. The CC0 one is 1280x720.

name: BasketBar
features: Campus café and bookshop with a full basketball court on its roof, the café floor sunk below the square.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2005, Emerging Architect special mention
note: Only one photo on Commons.

name: La Borda
features: Resident-owned cooperative housing in cross-laminated timber around a covered central courtyard.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2022, Emerging Architecture winner

photos.file: File:La Borda building - rear facade, whole building.jpg
File:La Borda etxebizitza kooperatibaren hegoaldeko fatxada.jpg
File:La Borda building - rear facade in context.jpg

note: The 'front facade' files in the category seem to show the neighbouring street front, not La Borda itself; I left them out.

name: Biblioteca Gabriel García Márquez
features: Stacked, shifted floors around a top-lit atrium, built in timber and wrapped in vertical metal fins.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2024, Emerging Architecture winner

photos.file: File:162 Biblioteca Gabriel García Márquez, c. Treball 219 (Barcelona), angle nord-est.jpg
File:171 Biblioteca Gabriel García Márquez, c. Treball 219 (Barcelona), angle nord-oest.jpg
File:165 Biblioteca Gabriel García Márquez, c. Treball 219 - c. Concili de Trento (Barcelona).jpg

note: Good interior series too (files 170-181).

name: NAVEZ, 5 social housing units
features: Five social flats for large families in a slim corner block at the northern entrance to Brussels.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2017, Emerging Architect winner
note: Corner of rue Navez and rue Portaels, Schaerbeek. Completion year from memory (2016); check.

name: Selfridges Building, Birmingham
features: Department store as a curving blob, its blue skin covered in 15,000 spun aluminium discs.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2005 finalist
note: Type is a department store; vocab has no retail type, so Workplace.

name: Zénith de Strasbourg
features: Concert hall wrapped in orange textile membrane over elliptical steel rings that twist as they rise.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2009 finalist
note: In France (no freedom of panorama) but several photos have survived. Strasbourg-Eckbolsheim.

name: Rivesaltes Camp Memorial
features: Long concrete monolith sunk into the old camp, its roof no higher than the ruined barracks around it.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2017 finalist
note: Weak: the one exterior photo shows the flat roof barely above the ground among the barracks, which is the building's point but reads faintly. Files 4 and 5 of the same series are interiors; 1-3 show the barracks only. If the owner wants a clearer image this is a good drawing candidate.

name: Kannikegården
features: Parish house beside Ribe Cathedral; steep roofs and walls wrapped in one skin of brick, over medieval ruins.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2017 finalist
note: The ruins under the building are visible inside; photos of them are in the category.

name: Katyń Museum
features: Museum in a 19th-century citadel fort; a narrow stair cuts straight through the earth rampart.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2017 finalist
commons_category: Category:Exterior of the Katyń Museum in Warsaw

photos.file: File:PL Wwa, Muz Katyn, 2024.08.29, fot Ivonna Nowicka (3) CORR.jpg

note: Parent Category:Katyn Museum in Warsaw also has many interior photos (2023 series). Opening year from memory; check.

name: Saw Swee Hock Student Centre, LSE
features: Faceted brick block shaped by the narrow streets around it, with perforated brick screens over its windows.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2015 finalist
commons_category: Category:LSE Saw Swee Hock Student Centre

photos.file: File:Saw Swee Hock Student Centre, LSE 02.jpg

name: Kunstmuseum Ravensburg
features: Museum walled in reclaimed brick, its roof a row of brick vaults that shows as a wavy parapet.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2015 finalist

name: Scientific Information Centre and Academic Library (CINiBA)
features: Seven-storey library clad in red sandstone panels with narrow windows set into the pattern, echoing campus brick.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2015 finalist
note: Cladding material (red sandstone) from memory; check.

name: Stadshal (Market Hall), Ghent
by: Robbrecht en Daem, Marie-José Van Hee
features: Open hall of twin steep timber-clad roofs on concrete legs among Ghent's towers; light pierces the wooden ceiling.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2013 finalist
note: Many more photos in the category, inside and out.

name: Centro de Artes de Sines
features: Stone-clad blocks on both sides of a street, linked below ground; a glazed base opens to the pavement.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2007 finalist

photos.file: File:Centro de Artes de Sines, Sines 01.jpg
File:Centro de Artes de Sines - Portugal (6539042727).jpg
File:Centro de Artes de Sines, Sines 02.jpg

name: Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision
features: Cube of coloured glass printed with TV images in relief; half the building, the archive, is sunk below ground.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2009 finalist
note: Only one exterior photo found by search (2000x1333); the institute's Commons category may hold more. Facade glass by Jaap Drupsteen.

name: Groot Klimmendaal Rehabilitation Centre
features: Rehabilitation centre in woodland: long dark volumes stacked and cantilevered over the slope, full of daylight.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2011 finalist
note: Two photos only, both partly behind trees.

name: Z33 House for Contemporary Art, Design and Architecture
features: A long, almost blind wall of red brick in relief patterns; inside, a sequence of rooms of different sizes.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2022 finalist

photos.file: File:Z33 Huis voor Acuele Kunst, Design & Architectuur foto door Olmo Peeters.jpg
File:Z33 Huis voor Actuele Kunst, Design & Architectuur Voorgevel foto door Olmo Peeters.jpg

note: Older 2016 files in the category show the site before the extension.

name: PLATO Contemporary Art Gallery
features: Old municipal slaughterhouse turned art gallery; new concrete panels fill and open its old door and window holes.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2024 finalist

photos.file: File:Ostrava, Městská jatka - galerie Plato po přestavbě (květen 2022) 01.jpg
File:Ostrava, Městská jatka - galerie Plato po přestavbě (květen 2022) 02.jpg

note: Interior photos (2022) in the same series.

name: Mortensrud Church
features: Steel-and-glass church lined with dry-stacked slate walls; the bare bedrock rises through the floor.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003 finalist
note: Many interior photos in the category.

name: Terrassenhaus Berlin / Lobe Block
by: Brandlhuber+ Emde, Burlon and Muck Petzet Architekten
features: Raw concrete frame stepping back in deep terraces, with an open outdoor stair climbing the stepped side.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2019 finalist
note: Only one photo (1272x1000), credited to photographer Erica Overmeer; worth checking the upload is hers or licensed by her. Living and working building in Berlin-Wedding.

name: Hedge House
features: Concrete and glass art pavilion in the garden of Kasteel Wijlre, set low between tall hedges.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003 finalist
note: Completion year from memory; check.

name: Rebirth of the Convent Saint-François
features: A perforated copper volume rebuilds the lost north wing of a 1480 Franciscan convent, roof included.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2024 finalist
note: Commons photos (2006-2019) all predate the 2021 extension, so they show the old ruin, not the awarded work. Not drawn: sources say the copper volume follows the old north wing and covers its roof, but I could not pin down its storeys and openings. France has no freedom of panorama. Year from memory.

name: The Railway Farm (La Ferme du Rail)
features: Timber buildings with rooftop greenhouses beside the old Petite Ceinture railway: housing, a farm and a restaurant.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2022 finalist
note: No Commons photos found (France has no freedom of panorama). Not drawn: I could not establish the massing from reachable sources. Facts from memory; check.

name: Reggio School
by: Andrés Jaque / Office for Political Innovation
features: School stacked as a vertical sequence of environments, its irregular exterior coated in sprayed cork.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2024 finalist
note: No Commons photos found. Not drawn: the massing is irregular and I could not establish it with confidence. Cork coating from memory; check.

name: Enrico Fermi School
features: A 1960s school reworked and opened to its neighbourhood, with new shared spaces at ground level.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2022, Emerging Architecture finalist
note: No Commons photos found (Italy has no freedom of panorama). Not drawn: form not established. Year and description from memory; check.

name: Collage House
features: An old town house in Girona rebuilt by layering new rooms, patios and light wells into the old stone walls.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2011, Emerging Architect special mention
note: No Commons photos. Not drawn: the work is mostly inside an existing house; the exterior is not documented in reachable sources. Year from memory.

name: Casa Luz
features: A village stone house in Extremadura hollowed out around a bright central space.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2015, Emerging Architect special mention
note: No Commons photos. Not drawn: exterior not documented in reachable sources. Year and description from memory; check.

name: Gymnasium, Koprivnica
features: A secondary school and sports hall combined in one long building that the town also uses.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2009, Emerging Architect special mention
note: No Commons photos found. Not drawn: form not established from reachable sources. Year and description from memory; check.

name: Kaufmann Holz Distribution Centre
features: A large timber warehouse for a timber firm, built quickly and cheaply from simple prefabricated parts.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2001, Emerging Architect special mention
note: No Commons photos found. Not drawn: form not established from reachable sources. Year and description from memory; check.

name: Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics
features: Faculty building for mathematics in central Ljubljana by a then-young Slovenian office.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2007, Emerging Architect special mention
note: No Commons photo of this building (the architects' category holds others). Not drawn: form not established. Facts beyond the award are from memory; check.

name: School Canteen, Montbrun-Bocage
features: Village school canteen of cross-laminated timber panels and black-framed glass on a sanded concrete plinth.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2019, Emerging Architecture winner
note: No Commons photos (France has no freedom of panorama). Not drawn: materials are described, but not the roof shape or massing. Completion year not found.

name: Antinori nel Chianti Classico Winery
features: Winery buried in a vineyard hill; only two long horizontal cuts in the slope show the building.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2015 finalist
view: Elevation of the vineyard hill from the valley: the two horizontal incisions (glazed terraces under the planted roof), vine rows following the contours
note: No usable free exterior photo: Commons has one distant landscape view (File:Bargino.jpg, 1600x1200, CC BY-SA 3.0) where the winery is a faint band, and interior shots (File:Angoli e geometrie.jpg, File:Looking up (Unsplash).jpg, the spiral stair). Italy has no freedom of panorama. Glazing divisions are schematic.

name: Fisterra Cemetery
features: Granite boxes scattered down the cliff above the Atlantic, linked by paths, with no enclosing wall.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003 finalist
view: Side elevation of the slope falling to the sea, with a line of the granite boxes sitting on it
note: No Commons photos found. Drawing is schematic: a local listing says 14 granite cubes; six are shown, as one elevation would see them, and their spacing and sizes are illustrative. Openings left out because I could not confirm their shape. Sources disagree on dates (built c. 1997-2002); never used for burials. Owner may prefer to mark it unsure.
